precepts.text: John the Baptist said to the Pharisees and Sadducees, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance: God's commandments in application are what prove repentance.
precepts.point: The way of peace they know not; and there is no judgment in their goings: they have made them crooked paths; whosoever goeth therein shall not know peace. You follow the Democratic or the Republican party, you follow the cross and the idols, you are not going to find peace. Our people have made crooked paths for themselves.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
Isaiah 59:5 says “They hatch cockatrice’ eggs”, and a cockatrice is like a poisonous snake. Put together everything from verses two to four, the iniquities that separated us from our God, the hands defiled with blood, the lips that have spoken lies, and this is what comes of it: “he that eateth of their eggs dieth, and that which is crushed breaketh out into a viper.” The eggs that are crushed are the kids that come out: a little baby snake. They produce evil followers.

Many years ago at a community meeting a black woman screamed at the police that they were selling drugs in her building and nobody was doing anything. The police set up a sting and locked up two dudes putting drugs in the mailboxes: her own sons. Then she came back saying it was false, with them on video. These are the eggs, the snake eggs coming out.

John the Baptist saw the same thing: “But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers”. That is the same thing Isaiah was talking about. “who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance”.

A generation of vipers cannot just say it repents. You have to bring forth God's commandments in application; that is what proves your repentance.

precepts.text: I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance. If baptism automatically meant water, why would John need to say I baptize you with water? Water baptism was John's administration, a tool to show forth repentance; it was never a requirement for the kingdom. He that cometh after me is mightier than I: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire. Did you hear anything about water? The baptism we must come under is through Christ.
precepts.point: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body. A video of a church baptism in a filthy pond was shown, and the teachers had some fun with it, but this verse is not talking about getting dunked in water. Baptized means cleanse; write that down and look it up yourself. Baptized does not automatically mean dipped in water; that is what a lot of Southern Baptists think.

note.label: Members of the Body  Pt2

precepts.why:
“For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body”. How many of us were dunked in water, the Baptist way? A church baptism in a green, filthy pond was shown, the brothers joking that it was pickle juice, but this verse is not talking about that. Baptized means cleanse. Write that down and look it up yourself: baptized does not automatically mean dipped in water, which is what a lot of Southern Baptists think.

John says: “I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance”. If baptism always meant water, why would he need to say, I baptize you with water? It means, I cleanse you with water unto repentance. That was John's administration, water baptism, a tool to show forth repentance. It was never a requirement for the kingdom of heaven.

“but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear”. Somebody far mightier is coming, whose shoes John is not even worthy to hold. “he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire”. Did you hear anything about water? No. The baptism we must come under is through Christ: by one Spirit we are all cleansed into one body.

precepts.text: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.
precepts.point: And I will cause you to pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant: and I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me. Even after; even after the deliverance, there is still going to be a purge. There will still be bad actors among us that need to be purged, people that still need to get right, and Christ is the one who is going to give it to them. They shall not enter into the land of Israel: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.

note.label: Forged by Fire

precepts.why:
Ezekiel says, “And I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me”. What kind of purge is he going to be doing? Killing. Matthew shows it: “Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.” Does anybody not understand that?

The wheat is gathered into the garner, and the chaff is burned. That is the rebels who “shall not enter into the land of Israel”. Zechariah is still talking about the purge: “in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.” And even the third that is left still has to be sifted, refined, made right, purged.

The Lord is not going to give the kingdom to wicked negroes. The kingdom will not be open to wicked negroes. To get the kingdom you have to go through this fire and get right; there is no other way. You can't keep doing what you do and think you are going to get the kingdom. It is impossible.

That is why we have to fight for this and help each other. If I see you weak and say nothing to you, that means I hate you. So if I tell you, bro, you have to fix that, and you say I hate you, shut your ass up; I am trying to save your life. We are so used to not taking correction from each other that it feels like hate, because everybody has coddled you, and you keep kicking the can down the street until you are back on the corner doing what you do. The fan is already in his hand.

precepts.text: Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him. The same Jordan, the number and the river pointing to the same Christ.
precepts.point: Who did the healing? The spirit of Christ, working through Elisha. What healed Naaman was his belief and his obedience to the word of the prophet.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him.” Christ went unto John the Baptist to be baptized, and in what river? Jordan: the same river that Naaman had to dip in seven times.

Seven represents completion. Naaman dipped seven times in Jordan, completion in the river Jordan, and his flesh came again like the flesh of a little child. The number and the river both point to the same Christ.

Who did the healing for Naaman? Not Elisha on his own. Elisha was working by the spirit of Christ; Christ is the one who did the healing, and he used Elisha as the prophet. So when Christ himself comes to the Jordan, it is the same one who cleansed Naaman there, the one who makes us clean.

precepts.text: Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand; bring forth fruits meet for repentance.
precepts.point: The Pharisees asked why Christ ate with publicans and sinners, the same spirit as the Pharisee in Luke 18. They that be whole need not a physician: the law is not made for the righteous but for the sick, the lawless and whoremongers. I will have mercy and not sacrifice, from Hosea, and I am come to call sinners to repentance.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
The Lord is “the God of them that repent”, and repentance is the first thing preached when the kingdom draws near: “Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” It was the first thing Christ said in his preaching, and it goes for all of us.

John the Baptist cried it: “For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.” He wore “raiment of camel’s hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey.” And “Jerusalem, and all Judea, and all the region round about Jordan” came out and were baptized of him in Jordan, “confessing their sins.”

“But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?” What are you doing here? “Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance”: fruits suitable for repentance.

That is the fig tree in Luke 13, dunged and dug about so that it may bring forth fruit. That was John’s ministry, paving the way for Christ. Manasseh did not only say sorry; he confessed his sins and his life changed. That is repentance with fruit.

precepts.text: John baptized with water, but Christ baptizes with the Holy Ghost and fire.
precepts.point: It is impossible to renew to repentance those who fall away after being enlightened.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
The doctrine of baptisms Hebrews 6 says to leave includes John the Baptist. John said it himself: “I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire”.

John used water. Christ baptizes with the Holy Ghost and with fire, not using water. Christ never used water, because water baptism was to end. It was always symbolic.

So when Paul says “let us go on unto perfection”, the baptism we go on to is Christ's, with the Holy Ghost and fire. The water was part of the principles we leave behind.

precepts.text: John is the voice of one crying in the wilderness, prepare ye the way of the Lord.
precepts.point: All flesh is grass and its goodliness as the flower of the field; the grass withers and the flower fades, but the word of our God stands forever. It compares our lives to the flowers of the field: we are born, we grow, we die, and go back into the ground, but the word of the Most High is forever.

note.label: Isaiah 40: Comfort My People and the Everlasting God

precepts.why:
Matthew names the voice: “For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.” John is the voice of one crying in the wilderness, prepare ye the way of the Lord, the one Isaiah spoke of.

So Isaiah 40:3 is the prophecy of John, the spirit of Elijah, preparing the way for the Lord: every valley exalted, every mountain and hill made low, the crooked made straight and the rough places plain, so that the glory of the Lord shall be revealed and all flesh see it together, “for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.”

precepts.text: Bring forth fruits meet for repentance, for the axe is laid to the root of every tree that does not.
precepts.point: The tree represents Israel, and once the word spreads we know how to bring forth fruit.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
By the river grow “all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed”, bringing forth new fruit according to their months, “because their waters they issued out of the sanctuary”. The tree represents Israel, and its fruit comes from the water, the word.

“Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance”. The axe is laid to the root of every tree that does not. Once the word spreads, we know how to bring forth fruit: fruits meet for repentance, new fruit every month, leaf that does not fade, because our waters issued out of the sanctuary.

precepts.text: Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me.
precepts.point: John the Baptist preaches in the wilderness of Judea, saying repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. He is the messenger the prophets said would go before the Lord, coming in the spirit of Elijah.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
John the Baptist came preaching in the wilderness of Judea, “Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” He is the messenger the prophets said would go before the Lord: “Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me”.

Malachi says that after the messenger prepares the way, “the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom ye delight in”. John is the messenger sent ahead; the Lord who follows him is Christ, the messenger of the covenant. John's preaching of repentance in the wilderness is the preparing of that way.

precepts.text: I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord.
precepts.point: John the Baptist preaches in the wilderness of Judea, saying repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. He is the messenger the prophets said would go before the Lord, coming in the spirit of Elijah.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
The messenger who goes before the Lord comes in the spirit of Elijah: “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.”

John the Baptist is that Elijah, sent before the Lord, turning hearts by preaching “Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” Malachi 3:1 tells of the messenger; Malachi 4:5-6 tells whose spirit he would come in. John fits both, preaching in the wilderness of Judea before Christ came to his temple.

precepts.text: The prophecy John fulfilled, word for word.
precepts.point: The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, is Isaiah's word spoken of John.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
Matthew says John “is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias”, and here is Isaiah's word, fulfilled word for word: “The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.”

John was that voice crying in the wilderness of Judea, preparing the way of the Lord. Isaiah goes on: “Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low: and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough places plain: And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.”

The mouth of the Lord spoke it through Isaiah, and John came and fulfilled it.

precepts.text: He was an hairy man, and girt with a girdle of leather about his loins; and he said, It is Elijah the Tishbite.
precepts.point: His raiment of camel's hair and the leathern girdle about his loins are not incidental. That was Elijah's manner, and it marks John as coming in the same spirit.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
John's raiment of camel's hair and the leathern girdle about his loins are not incidental. When the messengers described the man who met them, “He was an hairy man, and girt with a girdle of leather about his loins”, the king knew at once: “It is Elijah the Tishbite.”

That was Elijah's manner, the hairy garment and the girdle of leather about his loins. John wore the same, and it marks him as coming in the same spirit, the Elijah sent before the coming of the Lord.

precepts.text: That they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.
precepts.point: The fruits meet for repentance are works, not offerings brought to cover sin.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
When John saw the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism he called them a generation of vipers and told them, “Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance”. Paul preached the same thing, to Damascus, Jerusalem, all the coasts of Judea and then to the Gentiles: “that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.”

The fruits meet for repentance are works. Repentance is turning to God and doing works, not offerings brought to cover sin. That is what John demanded of the Pharisees and Sadducees, and what Paul preached everywhere he went.

precepts.text: I know that ye are Abraham's seed; but ye seek to kill me, because my word hath no place in you.
precepts.point: Descent from Abraham without the works of Abraham counts for nothing. The works of Abraham are believing the Most High and keeping his commandments.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
John warned them, “think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father”. Christ met the same boast. He did not deny their descent: “I know that ye are Abraham’s seed; but ye seek to kill me, because my word hath no place in you.”

They were Abraham's seed and still sought to kill him, because his word had no place in them. Being of Abraham's seed did not make them Abraham's children in the way that counts. Descent from Abraham without the works of Abraham counts for nothing, which is why John said the Most High could raise up children unto Abraham from stones.

precepts.text: If ye were Abraham's children, ye would do the works of Abraham.
precepts.point: Descent from Abraham without the works of Abraham counts for nothing. The works of Abraham are believing the Most High and keeping his commandments.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
They answered Christ, “Abraham is our father”, the very thing John told them not to say within themselves. Christ answered, “If ye were Abraham’s children, ye would do the works of Abraham.”

Being Abraham's children is proven by doing the works of Abraham, not by the blood alone. They had the descent but not the works, so the claim was empty. John's warning and Christ's answer are the same teaching.

precepts.text: Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws; that is the work of Abraham.
precepts.point: Descent from Abraham without the works of Abraham counts for nothing. The works of Abraham are believing the Most High and keeping his commandments.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
What are the works of Abraham? The Most High says it plainly: “Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.” That is the work of Abraham: believing the Most High and keeping his commandments, his statutes and his laws.

So a child of Abraham is one who does what Abraham did, obeying the voice of the Most High and keeping his commandments. Those who had Abraham to their father in the flesh but did not keep his charge could not lean on that descent. That is why John told the Pharisees and Sadducees not to think it, and why God is able of stones to raise up children unto Abraham.

precepts.text: Jesus himself baptized not, but his disciples.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost is bound to the law. To resist the Holy Ghost is to resist the commandments, and the Comforter brings the words of Christ to remembrance.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
John said plainly, “I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I”, and that one “shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire”. John's water baptism is not the baptism of the one coming after him.

That is why, when the Pharisees heard that Jesus made and baptized more disciples than John, the scripture adds, “Though Jesus himself baptized not, but his disciples”. Christ himself did not baptize with water. Water was John's baptism; Christ's baptism is the Holy Ghost and fire.

precepts.text: Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, was first a disciple of John, which is how water baptism carried on among some of the disciples.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost is bound to the law. To resist the Holy Ghost is to resist the commandments, and the Comforter brings the words of Christ to remembrance.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
How did water baptism carry on among some of the disciples if Christ himself baptized not? “One of the two which heard John speak, and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.” Andrew was first a disciple of John before he followed Christ.

Water baptism was what John did, and disciples who came from John carried it on. That does not make it the baptism Christ gives. His baptism, as John said, is with the Holy Ghost and with fire.

precepts.text: Ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost is bound to the law. To resist the Holy Ghost is to resist the commandments, and the Comforter brings the words of Christ to remembrance.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
The Holy Ghost that Christ baptizes with is bound to the law. Stephen told the council, “Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.”

Their fathers resisted the Holy Ghost, and they did the same. To understand what the baptism of the Holy Ghost is, we have to see what resisting the Holy Ghost is, and Stephen tells it in the verses that follow.

precepts.text: What the fathers resisted was the law, received by the disposition of angels and not kept.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost is bound to the law. To resist the Holy Ghost is to resist the commandments, and the Comforter brings the words of Christ to remembrance.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
Stephen says what the fathers resisted: “Who have received the law by the disposition of angels, and have not kept it.” They received the law by the disposition of angels and did not keep it. That is resisting the Holy Ghost.

So the Holy Ghost is bound to the law. To resist the Holy Ghost is to resist the commandments. The baptism of the Holy Ghost that Christ gives, mightier than John's water, is not apart from the law but joined to it.

precepts.text: If ye love me, keep my commandments, and the Comforter follows.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost is bound to the law. To resist the Holy Ghost is to resist the commandments, and the Comforter brings the words of Christ to remembrance.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
Christ says, “If ye love me, keep my commandments.” Keeping the commandments comes first, and the Comforter follows. The Holy Ghost is bound to the law: the one who loves Christ keeps his commandments, and to him the Comforter is sent.

This is the baptism John pointed to, with the Holy Ghost and with fire, and it is not given to those who resist the commandments.

precepts.text: The Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, shall teach you all things and bring all things to your remembrance.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost is bound to the law. To resist the Holy Ghost is to resist the commandments, and the Comforter brings the words of Christ to remembrance.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
Christ tells what the Comforter does: “But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.”

The Comforter is the Holy Ghost, and his work is to teach and to bring the words of Christ to remembrance. It comes after “If ye love me, keep my commandments.” So the baptism of the Holy Ghost that Christ gives is the Father sending the Comforter in Christ's name to those who keep his commandments, teaching them and bringing his words back to their minds.

precepts.text: The words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost is bound to the law. To resist the Holy Ghost is to resist the commandments, and the Comforter brings the words of Christ to remembrance.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
What are the words the Comforter brings to remembrance? Christ says, “It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.”

His words are spirit and life. The Holy Ghost brings those words to remembrance, and those words are bound to the law he told us to keep. That is the baptism mightier than water that John spoke of: the spirit that quickens by the words of Christ, not the flesh, which profits nothing.

precepts.text: The ungodly are like the chaff which the wind driveth away.
precepts.point: He will gather his wheat into the garner and burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire. There are two baptisms in view, and everyone receives one of them.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
John says of the one coming after him, “he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.” Who is the chaff? “The ungodly are not so: but are like the chaff which the wind driveth away.”

The ungodly are the chaff. There are two baptisms in view, the Holy Ghost and fire, and everyone receives one of them. The wheat is gathered into the garner; the chaff, the ungodly, is driven away and burned up with unquenchable fire.

precepts.text: The Most High shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie.
precepts.point: The one in the water and the voice out of heaven are not the same. There is the Father, and there is his son.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
Christ went up out of the water, the Spirit of the Most High descended like a dove and lit upon him, and a voice out of the heavens said, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.” The one in the water and the voice out of heaven are not the same. There is the Father, and there is his son.

Those who will not see that have been given over to it: “And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.” The Most High sends strong delusion on those who believe not the truth, and they believe a lie.

Here at the baptism the truth is plain: the Father speaks from heaven of his beloved Son standing in the water. To make them one and the same is the lie, and it comes on those who had pleasure in unrighteousness rather than the truth.

precepts.text: John baptized with water unto repentance, but he that came after him would baptize with the Holy Ghost and with fire.
precepts.point: John said he must decrease and Christ must increase, and that happens in increments. Two of John's own disciples heard Christ and followed him, which is why in Acts the disciples were still baptizing with water even though Christ himself baptized not with water but with the Holy Ghost. When you believe on Christ as the scripture says, rivers of living water flow out of your belly, meaning wisdom and understanding flow out of the mind that consumes and filters information; but that Holy Ghost was not yet given because Jesus was not yet glorified.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“For John truly baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost not many days hence.” There is a distinction between what John taught and what Christ brought.

John said it himself: “I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire.” John's water baptism was always symbolic, a preparation leading up to Christ. Baptism comes from the word baptizo, out of the purification laws.

John said he must decrease and Christ must increase, and that happens in increments.

precepts.text: John baptized with water unto repentance, but he that cometh after shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost.
precepts.point: The gift of the Holy Ghost that follows is understanding being opened. Baptism with the Holy Ghost is the spirit of wisdom and understanding, seen when Christ opened the disciples' understanding to grasp the scriptures concerning him.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
John said, “I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire”. Water unto repentance, and then the baptism of the Holy Ghost from Christ.

Repent means sin no more, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins. It is done in the name of Jesus because Christ was not fully known then; the people had followed animal sacrifice, so now they had to believe on his name.

The gift of the Holy Ghost that follows is the baptism John spoke of: understanding being opened. Baptism with the Holy Ghost is the spirit of wisdom and understanding.

precepts.text: John said, I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance, but he that cometh after me shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost; the water baptism came from the purification and water of separation in Numbers chapter 19.
precepts.point: Then the apostles laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Ghost, after they had repented and believed in Christ. There are two different baptisms: John's water baptism, which came from the Levitical purification laws and was symbolic of repentance, and Christ's baptism with the Holy Ghost, which is the laws and the cleansing of the conscience. Water can only wash the dirt off the skin; it cannot clean the evil in your mind. Christ magnified the law within the conscience, showing that sin starts in the mind, so his cleansing purifies your consciousness through his word.

John's water baptism came from the Levitical purification laws, the purification and water of separation in Numbers chapter 19, and it was symbolic of repentance. Christ's baptism is with the Holy Ghost.

When the apostles laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Ghost, that is Christ's baptism, given after they had repented and believed in Christ. Water can only wash the dirt off the skin; it cannot clean the evil in your mind.

points: John the Baptist preaches in the wilderness of Judea, saying repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. He is the messenger the prophets said would go before the Lord, coming in the spirit of Elijah.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

points: The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, is Isaiah's word spoken of John.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

points: His raiment of camel's hair and the leathern girdle about his loins are not incidental. That was Elijah's manner, and it marks John as coming in the same spirit.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

points: They were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins. Confession of sin is part of what is happening here, not a bare dipping in water.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

points: To the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism John says, O generation of vipers, bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance.
The fruits meet for repentance are works, not offerings brought to cover sin.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

points: Do not say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father. The Most High is able of stones to raise up children unto Abraham.
Descent from Abraham without the works of Abraham counts for nothing. The works of Abraham are believing the Most High and keeping his commandments.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

points: Every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down and cast into the fire. Christ says the same thing again later in this gospel.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

points: John says plainly that his water baptism is not the baptism of the one coming after him. That one shall baptize with the Holy Ghost and with fire.
The Holy Ghost is bound to the law. To resist the Holy Ghost is to resist the commandments, and the Comforter brings the words of Christ to remembrance.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

points: He will gather his wheat into the garner and burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire. There are two baptisms in view, and everyone receives one of them.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

points: Christ comes to John to be baptized, and when John forbids him he answers, Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

points: Christ comes up out of the water, the Spirit of the Most High descends like a dove, and a voice out of the heavens says, This is my beloved son, in whom I am well pleased.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

points: The one in the water and the voice out of heaven are not the same. There is the Father, and there is his son.
